answer: Escrowed uniqueness proof:** Each new identity must submit a fresh cipher proving work over a per-epoch challenge, and the result is checked against a public trellis of already-claimed solutions. Duplicates and near-duplicates are rejected because the challenge space narrows each epoch, so a clone must outcompute the current horizon of valid solutions. Cost: repeated proof generation plus forfeited escrow on collision, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
